scenario.name: AWS CIRT, Datadog & MITRE — AWS STS GetFederationToken Console Sign-In Bypass & IAM Policy Audit
scenario.overview: Imagine a cloud bank where a thief steals a long-lived machine delivery badge designed only for automated back-door shipping, not for walking through the executive web lobby. Using a special exchange counter, the thief trades that machine badge for a federated visitor pass, exchanges the pass at the lobby ticket booth for a live browser wristband, and strolls straight into the graphical management console to read every security policy on screen. In this scenario (T1550.001, AWS CIRT, Datadog & MITRE, AWS STS GetFederationToken Console Sign-In Bypass & IAM Policy Audit), the attacker follows one continuous intrusion path so each later Step can show the exact handoff that makes the next stage possible. The attack unfolds in one continuous arc: programmatic AKIA Access Key Invocation, then federation SigninToken Exchange, then console Reconnaissance. Steps #1–#3 walk that chain end-to-end by covering Programmatic AKIA Access Key Invocation, then Federation SigninToken Exchange, then Console Reconnaissance, while the Process Hierarchy tab keeps the Parent → Child spawn tree visible so you can see which trusted process launched the next payload. Primary detection pivots on CloudTrail Event 200 correlated across the documented kill chain.

specs.value: Remove inline sts:GetFederationToken permissions from IAM Users, migrate from static AKIA keys to IAM Roles Anywhere or SSO, and alert on GetFederationToken calls in CloudTrail.

stages.title: Stage 1: Programmatic AKIA Access Key Invocation of sts:GetFederationToken
stages.subtitle: Defense Evasion (T1550.001 - Use Alternate Authentication Material: Application Access Token)
stages.description: Holding a leaked static programmer key meant solely for automated scripts, the intruder calls the cloud token-exchange counter asking for a federated session pass that can bridge into interactive web access. Holding a long-lived IAM User access key (AKIA...), the actor calls sts:GetFederationToken to mint temporary federated credentials (ASIA...) scoped to an inline session policy, logged in AWS CloudTrail (logged in Linux Audit Event 200 with EventSource=sts.amazonaws.com, EventName=GetFederationToken, PrincipalUser=ci-deploy-bot , AKIAIOSFODNN7EXAMPLE so analysts can verify the exact actor and target artifact). Under the hood, the observed step executes aws cloudtrail lookup-events --lookup-attributes AttributeKey=EventName,AttributeValue=GetFederationToken (which executes a cloud control-plane API or CLI operation , aws cloudtrail lookup-events --lookup-attributes AttributeKey=EventName,AttributeValue=GetFed so that harvests cloud identity tokens, escalates IAM privileges, or exfiltrates cloud data , T1550.001 during "Programmatic AKIA Access Key Invocation of sts:GetFederationToken" without deploying traditional endpoint malware, captured in CloudTrail / Unified Audit Log telemetry). Next, the follow-up artifact jq '.Records[] | select(.eventName=="GetFederationToken")' cloudtrail.json runs (which executes the technical command / telemetry directive , jq '.Records[] | select.eventName=="GetFederationToken"' cloudtrail.json via System / Runt so that advances the scenario kill-chain under MITRE T1550.001 during "Programmatic AKIA Access Key Invocation of sts:GetFederationToken" , Holding a long-lived IAM User access key , AKIA, the actor calls sts:GetFederationToken to mint temporary federated credentials , ASIA scoped to an inline session policy, logged in AWS CloudTrail while generating verifiable host or network telemetry for DFIR attribution). On the diagram, follow Step #1 / Link #1 (#1→ aws sts get-federation-token --name console-broker-session / ⇠#1 ACK 200) from Node ① (#1 External CLI Client (Leaked AKIA Key)) to Node ② (#2 Perimeter Firewall & NDR Tap), monitored by Node ⑥ (#6 AWS Management Console & IAM API).

stages.title: Stage 2: Federation SigninToken Exchange & Interactive ConsoleLogin Event
stages.subtitle: Lateral Movement (T1078.004 - Valid Accounts: Cloud Accounts)
stages.description: Handing that temporary federated pass straight to the web lobby ticket booth, the intruder receives a single-use browser entry link and logs smoothly into the interactive graphical console without ever needing a user password or MFA token. The actor passes the temporary federated credentials to https://signin.aws.amazon.com/federation?Action=getSigninToken and opens the resulting Console login URL, producing a ConsoleLogin CloudTrail event with userIdentity.type="FederatedUser" and additionalEventData.MFAUsed="No" (logged in Linux Audit Event 200 with EventName=ConsoleLogin, IdentityType=FederatedUser , sts:GetFederationToken, MfaStatus=MFAUsed: No so analysts can verify the exact actor and target artifact). Under the hood, the observed step executes jq '.Records[] | select(.eventName=="ConsoleLogin" and .userIdentity.type=="FederatedUser")' cloudtrail.json (which executes the technical command / telemetry directive , jq '.Records[] | select.eventName=="ConsoleLogin" and .userIdentity.type=="FederatedUser"' so that advances the scenario kill-chain under MITRE T1078.004 during "Federation SigninToken Exchange & Interactive ConsoleLogin Event" , The actor passes the temporary federated credentials to https://signin while generating verifiable host or network telemetry for DFIR attribution). Next, the follow-up artifact aws guardduty list-findings --detector-id <id> runs (which executes a cloud control-plane API or CLI operation , aws guardduty list-findings --detector-id <id> against AWS CloudTrail, GCP Cloud Audit, or Mi so that harvests cloud identity tokens, escalates IAM privileges, or exfiltrates cloud data , T1078.004 during "Federation SigninToken Exchange & Interactive ConsoleLogin Event" without deploying traditional endpoint malware, captured in CloudTrail / Unified Audit Log telemetry). On the diagram, follow Step #2 / Link #2 (#2→ ConsoleLogin (FederatedUser: ci-deploy-bot/console-broker-session, MFAUsed=No) / ⇠#2 ACK 200) from Node ② (#2 Perimeter Firewall & NDR Tap) to Node ③ (#3 AWS STS Endpoint (GetFederationToken)), monitored by Node ⑥ (#6 AWS Management Console & IAM API).

keySpecs.value: Alert on any CloudTrail ConsoleLogin event where userIdentity.type is FederatedUser and MFAUsed is No, and attach an explicit Deny SCP for sts:GetFederationToken across member accounts.

stages.title: Stage 3: Console Reconnaissance & IAM Policy Version Enumeration Audit
stages.subtitle: Discovery (T1069.003 - Permission Groups Discovery: Cloud Groups)
stages.description: Now clicking freely through the visual web dashboards, the intruder inspects account blueprints and digs through older saved editions of company security policies hunting for over-privileged rules or hidden secrets. Inside the browser session, the federated identity queries IAM policies, S3 buckets, and Secrets Manager secrets, which defenders correlate via the shared principalId (<user_id>:console-broker-session) across CloudTrail management events (logged in Linux Audit Event 200 with CorrelatedSessionArn=arn:aws:sts::123456789012:federated-user/console-broker-session, EnumeratedApi=iam:GetAccountAuthorizationDetails, GuardDutyFinding=Policy:IAMUser/RootCredentialUsage so analysts can verify the exact actor and target artifact). Under the hood, the observed step executes jq '.Records[] | select(.userIdentity.arn | contains, "federated-user/console-broker-session")' cloudtrail.json (which executes the technical command / telemetry directive , jq '.Records[] | select.userIdentity.arn | contains, "federated-user/console-broker-sessio so that advances the scenario kill-chain under MITRE T1069.003 during "Console Reconnaissance & IAM Policy Version Enumeration Audit" , Inside the browser session, the federated identity queries IAM policies, S3 buckets, and Secrets Manager secrets, which defenders correlate via the shared principalId , <user_id>:console-broker-session across CloudTrail management events while generating verifiable host or network telemetry for DFIR attribution). Next, the follow-up artifact aws iam delete-access-key --user-name ci-deploy-bot --access-key-id AKIAIOSFODNN7EXAMPLE runs (which executes a cloud control-plane API or CLI operation , aws iam delete-access-key --user-name ci-deploy-bot --access-key-id AKIAIOSFODNN7EXAMPLE agai so that harvests cloud identity tokens, escalates IAM privileges, or exfiltrates cloud data , T1069.003 during "Console Reconnaissance & IAM Policy Version Enumeration Audit" without deploying traditional endpoint malware, captured in CloudTrail / Unified Audit Log telemetry). On the diagram, follow Step #3 / Link #3 (#3→ GetAccountAuthorizationDetails via Federated Console Session / ⇠#3 ACK 200) from Node ③ (#3 AWS STS Endpoint (GetFederationToken)) to Node ④ (#4 AWS Federation Signin Endpoint), monitored by Node ⑥ (#6 AWS Management Console & IAM API).

keySpecs.value: Deactivate the originating IAM User access key immediately and attach an inline Deny-All policy with a Condition on aws:TokenIssueTime to invalidate active STS federated sessions.
